findings.claim: `self.downsize` is defined twice in OptimizedImage. Ruby has no overloading, so the later (from, to, dimensions, opts) definition replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) one, and existing 5-argument callers such as ResizeEmoji (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) raise ArgumentError.

verifier.reason: The patch adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at app/models/optimized_image.rb:149, which replaces the 5-argument version at :145. That leaves a method taking 3–4 arguments, so the 5-argument call `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 raises ArgumentError.

findings.claim: API URL-based uploads now call FileHelper.download with a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. This ignores the configured limit: larger files are truncated or blocked on sites allowing more than 10 MB, and more than allowed is downloaded on sites with smaller limits.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 now calls FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) where it used to pass SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, so the configured limit is ignored. FileHelper.download stops reading once the file passes the cap (lib/file_helper.rb:18), so URL uploads over about 10 MB end up truncated even on sites that allow more; downloading past a smaller limit seems intended, since the new downsize loop shrinks the file afterwards.

findings.claim: Client-side upload validation hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for all upload types instead of using Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. Files the server will reject can pass the browser check, and files that sites configured above 10 MB allow are blocked.

verifier.reason: The patch changes app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 from Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] to a fixed 10 * 1024 for every upload type, and line 246 gets the same change. The server still checks each type against its own SiteSetting in lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81, so a file under 10 MB but over a smaller setting passes the browser check and is rejected by the server, and a file over 10 MB is blocked in the browser even when the site allows more.

findings.claim: The same 10 MB constant is duplicated in several places, so the client and server limits can drift apart.

verifier.reason: The patch hard-codes the 10 MB limit in three places: twice on the client (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 `10 * 1024` and :246 `10 * 1024`) and once on the server (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 `10.megabytes`). Nothing shares a constant or setting, so changing one would not update the others.

findings.claim: The HTTP 413 handler always reports a limit of 10240 KB, although the actual limit depends on the nginx/proxy client_max_body_size setting.

verifier.reason: The patch hardcodes `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10 MB` in the 413 case of app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js (~line 246), so the error message always shows 10240 KB. A 413 comes from the web server, and its limit is set by `client_max_body_size`: 10m in config/nginx.sample.conf:61 and 2m in docs/INSTALL-ubuntu.md:390, so the hardcoded value is wrong on some deployments.

findings.claim: The error message in displayErrorForUpload (line 246) shows a hardcoded 10 MB instead of the actual configured limit when the server rejects a file for exceeding a smaller configured limit.

verifier.reason: The patch changes the 413 branch of displayErrorForUpload so it always reports 10 * 1024 KB (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246); before, it used Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb. A 413 comes from the web server, whose limit an admin can set lower (docs/INSTALL-ubuntu.md:390 uses client_max_body_size 2m), so the message can state a wrong limit.

findings.claim: In the switch statement, `case 413` declares `maxSizeKB` without a surrounding block, so the declaration is visible to the other cases.

verifier.reason: At app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246, `maxSizeKB` is declared with `var`, so it belongs to the whole `displayErrorForUpload` function, and adding a block would not change that. No other case reads it, and the case-declaration hazard only applies to `let`/`const`/`class`/`function`, so nothing is actually wrong.

findings.claim: The downsize loop reads `tempfile.size`, which stays stale after the in-place downsize and ImageOptim rename. As a result, the loop may run all passes or fail to terminate correctly, and Upload.create_for receives a stale filesize, dimensions and a mismatched sha1.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-69 rewrites `tempfile.path` in place, using convert and then `ImageOptim.optimize_image!`, which does an atomic rename (app/models/optimized_image.rb:160-165). `tempfile.size` checks the open file handle, which still points at the old file, so the size stays stale: the loop can run all 5 passes (it always stops after 5) and `Upload.create_for` gets a stale filesize. `FastImage.new(file)` may also read stale dimensions through that handle, while the sha1 is computed from the path at upload.rb:106 and so does not match them. I inferred the rename from memory of the image_optim gem source, which is not in this repository.

findings.claim: Downsizing passes '80%' as the dimensions. For animated GIFs this goes to `gifsicle --resize-fit`, which accepts only WxH pixel geometry, so gifsicle fails and every retry attempt is used up.

verifier.reason: uploads_controller.rb:66 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. For a .gif path (API downloads keep the extension via lib/file_helper.rb:14), optimized_image.rb:155 routes this to downsize_instructions_animated → resize_instructions_animated, which builds `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` (optimized_image.rb:120). gifsicle only accepts WxH there, so the command fails every time and the loop at uploads_controller.rb:64-67 spends all 5 attempts without shrinking the file.

findings.claim: The allow_animation option is effectively dead code, because animated GIF downsizing fails through both upload paths.

verifier.reason: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (app/models/optimized_image.rb:149) replaces the 5-argument version at :145, so `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 raises ArgumentError even though it passes allow_animation: true. In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67, the Rack 1.5 upload tempfile path most likely has no .gif extension (from memory; I couldn't open the gem), so the animated branch at optimized_image.rb:155 is skipped; if it were taken, gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%` (:120) would fail because it needs WxH (also from memory). Note: allow_animation still works for resize (upload.rb:98, create_for); it is dead only for downsizing.

findings.claim: Each upload can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on files up to 10 MB.

verifier.reason: In uploads_controller.rb:63-67 the patch adds a loop that runs at most 5 times, calling OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%") while the file is still over max_image_size_kb. Each call goes through optimize/convert_with (optimized_image.rb:153-165), which runs a `convert` shell command (gifsicle for animated GIFs) and then ImageOptim.optimize_image!. The upload size limit is now a hardcoded 10 MB in utilities.js:182/246 and in FileHelper.download at uploads_controller.rb:55.

findings.claim: When OptimizedImage.downsize fails and returns false, the loop ignores the result, keeps retrying, and lets the oversized file continue.

verifier.reason: The return value of the downsize call at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 is never checked, so a failed convert is retried until the 5 attempts run out, and the oversized tempfile is then passed to Upload.create_for (line 72). The file is not stored, though: lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:84-86 still rejects files over max_image_size_kb, so the cost is up to 5 wasted ImageMagick runs and no clear error about why it failed.

findings.claim: The downsize loop shrinks the image to only about 33% of the original after 5 iterations (0.8^5), so an image can still exceed max_image_size_kb and proceed to Upload.create_for.

verifier.reason: The loop at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-70 stops after 5 tries of downsize "80%" and then calls Upload.create_for with whatever size the file has, so an oversized image does get there. The "33%" is off: 80% scales each side, so pixel area falls to about 0.64^5 ≈ 11%. The size check in lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-85 still rejects the file with a too_large error, so the limit is not bypassed.

findings.claim: Non-API uploads run in the shared Scheduler::Defer.later queue, so large uploads stall unrelated deferred work.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:19-22, any upload that isn't API-synchronous runs create_upload inside Scheduler::Defer.later, and lib/scheduler/defer.rb:5,55 serves that one shared Queue from a single thread. The patch adds up to five synchronous ImageMagick downsize passes on images of up to 10MB to that job (uploads_controller.rb:63-70), so a large upload holds up unrelated deferred work.

findings.claim: No tests cover the new downsize loop, the changed OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, or the client validation change.

verifier.reason: The patch adds no tests, and nothing in spec/ calls OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize or exercises the new loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-69 (spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb only stubs :resize). One part of the claim is slightly off: test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61 already exercises the client size check, but the patch does not update it, and with the limit hardcoded to 10MB that test (10KB file, max_image_size_kb=5) should now fail.

findings.claim: Image processing uses the same path for input and output, so the original file is lost if the operation fails mid-write.

verifier.reason: The patch adds a call at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 that passes `tempfile.path` as both input and output to OptimizedImage.downsize. That path goes straight to convert/gifsicle and then ImageOptim in app/models/optimized_image.rb:126-164, which overwrite the file in place with no temp file or backup, and the `false` return on failure is ignored, so a partial write leaves a corrupted file that is still uploaded.

findings.claim: With allow_animated_thumbnails off, `convert file[0]` writes only the first frame back over the original GIF.

verifier.reason: The new loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:41-46 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: false). That uses the non-animated downsize_instructions at app/models/optimized_image.rb:126-134, which runs `convert #{from}[0] ... #{to}` with from == to, so only the first frame is written back over the uploaded GIF. The animated path also needs a .gif path (optimized_image.rb:155), and the temp upload path may not have one, so the animation may be lost even with the setting on.

findings.claim: For regular browser uploads, Rack tempfile paths lack a .gif extension, so the GIF detection regex in optimize() never matches and `convert` with [0] strips animation from GIFs.

verifier.reason: In uploads_controller.rb:41-44 the patch calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...), and optimize() only uses the animated (gifsicle) path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (optimized_image.rb:77). Gemfile.lock pins rack 1.5.5, which I recall names multipart tempfiles `Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")` with no extension; I couldn't open the gem source here to check. So the regex fails and downsize_instructions runs `convert #{from}[0]` (optimized_image.rb:129), keeping only the first frame of an animated GIF.

findings.claim: The `tempfile &&` and `tempfile.size > 0` checks in the new guard are redundant with the loop condition and the later handling of a nil tempfile.

verifier.reason: Only `tempfile.size > 0` is redundant: with a size of 0 the loop condition at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 is false anyway. The `tempfile &&` check is not covered by anything. The loop condition calls `tempfile.size` with no nil check, and nothing later handles a nil tempfile, because line 72 calls `tempfile.size` directly. So the claim's reason is wrong.

findings.claim: FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, so oversized SVGs enter the downsize loop and ImageMagick rewrites the user's SVG in place.

verifier.reason: In lib/file_helper.rb:31, the `images` set includes "svg", so `is_image?` (line 5) returns true for .svg files. The new loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb (patch lines 41-46) therefore calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%")` on oversized SVGs, and `downsize_instructions` (app/models/optimized_image.rb:126-134) runs ImageMagick `convert ... -resize`, which writes its output over the uploaded file.

findings.claim: An inline `rescue nil` silently swallows all exceptions, including network errors.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 still has `FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil`. It swallows every StandardError, network failures included, and leaves `tempfile` nil, so line 72 (`tempfile.size`) later fails with a NoMethodError that hides the real cause. Strictly, it catches StandardError rather than literally every exception.
